paragraphs.name: ai-explainer-1
paragraphs.source: In today's rapidly evolving digital landscape, artificial intelligence has become an increasingly important tool for organizations of all sizes. It is important to note that the adoption of these technologies requires careful consideration of both the opportunities and the challenges involved. On the one hand, automation can significantly improve efficiency and reduce operational costs. On the other hand, organizations must ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place to protect user privacy and maintain trust. Furthermore, the ethical implications of these systems cannot be overlooked. By taking a balanced and thoughtful approach, organizations can harness the full potential of artificial intelligence while minimizing potential risks. Ultimately, success in this area depends on a commitment to transparency, accountability, and continuous improvement. As we move forward, it will be essential for stakeholders to work together to develop frameworks that support responsible innovation and deliver meaningful value to society as a whole.

paragraphs.name: ai-explainer-2
paragraphs.source: Climate change represents one of the most pressing challenges facing humanity in the twenty-first century. Rising global temperatures have led to a wide range of consequences, including more frequent extreme weather events, rising sea levels, and significant disruptions to ecosystems around the world. Addressing this challenge requires a multifaceted approach that combines technological innovation, policy reform, and changes in individual behaviour. Renewable energy sources such as solar and wind power play a significant role in reducing greenhouse gas emissions. At the same time, governments must implement policies that incentivize sustainable practices across industries. Education and public awareness also play a crucial role in driving meaningful change. In conclusion, while the challenges are substantial, a coordinated global effort offers the best path toward a more sustainable and resilient future for generations to come.
paragraphs.chosen: Climate change is the twenty-first century's slowest emergency: global temperatures are up about 1.2 degrees since 1850, most of it since 1975. The wars and droughts in Ukraine and Sudan have been caused by rising temperatures. Pakistan's 2022 floods displaced eight million people, sea levels rise about 3.7 millimetres a year, and extreme weather events that were once-a-century now recur within decades. Disruptions to ecosystems, like the 2016 Great Barrier Reef bleaching, get less attention than the storms. Renewable energy is the one part moving fast: solar and wind power supply about 13 percent of world electricity, up from 2 percent in 2010, and greenhouse gas emissions still rose in 2023. Governments price carbon on a quarter of emissions, most of it below 10 dollars a tonne, and few industries face real incentives for sustainable practices. Education and public awareness campaigns have run since the 1990s and individual behaviour has barely moved. A coordinated global effort was promised at Paris in 2015. The pledges still add up to about 2.7 degrees, which is not the future anyone described to the next generations.

paragraphs.source: Remote work has fundamentally transformed the way modern organizations operate. What began as a temporary response to unprecedented circumstances has evolved into a permanent fixture of the contemporary workplace. Employees increasingly value the flexibility that remote arrangements provide, and many report higher levels of job satisfaction as a result. However, this shift is not without its challenges. Maintaining team cohesion and organizational culture in a distributed environment requires intentional effort and robust communication practices. Managers must adapt their leadership styles to focus on outcomes rather than hours worked. Additionally, companies need to invest in the right tools and infrastructure to support seamless collaboration across time zones. By addressing these considerations proactively, organizations can create a hybrid model that delivers the best of both worlds.

It settled around 28 percent by 2023 and has stayed there. Remote work delivered much higher levels of job satisfaction and was broadly valued, with employees pricing flexibility at roughly an 8 percent pay rise. But the trade-off is tough. Maintaining cohesion and culture, and collaboration and relationships in a distributed environment requires explicit effort and awareness. Leadership needs to shift from an hours-worked focus to an outcomes-focused mindset. And companies must invest in the tools and infrastructure that allow distributed collaboration across time zones. By taking pro-active actions, companies can design the best-of-both-worlds approach.

paragraphs.source: Mutational processes are known to leave characteristic sequence features in the genomes. Well-recognized examples include C:G>A:T transversions and C:G>T:A transitions associated with the mutagens of tobacco smoking in lung cancers and ultraviolet radiation in skin cancers, respectively. The distinct sequence features of individual mutagenic processes indicate that the mutational processes that have been operative in cancer genomes can be inferred by sequence-based analyses. Accordingly, recently proposed trinucleotide context-based analysis of cancer genomes based on deconvolution techniques, such as non-negative matrix factorization (NMF), has revealed more than 30 mutations signatures across 7,000 cancer genomes (hereafter, Sig.#1 to Sig.#30 as annotated in the Sanger mutation signature database; https://cancer.sanger.ac.uk/cosmic/signatures). Signature-level mutation analysis enables the molecular dissection of TMB according to the distinct origins of the mutations because mutation signatures are often associated with causal genetic mechanisms or genes corresponding to endogenous mutagens and DNA repair-replication processes. For example, overactivity of APOBEC cytidine deaminase leads to the accumulation of mutations consistent with Sig.#2 and Sig.#13, with sequence preferences of C>G and C>T within the TpCpN trinucleotide contexts. Genetic events responsible for the deficiency of DNA repair enzymes have also been shown for some mutation signatures, e.g. somatic DNA mismatch repair deficiency (MMRd) in colorectal and endometrial cancers are frequently associated with promoter hypermethylation and transcriptional downregulation of MLH1. In addition, deregulation of DNA repair or the proofreading polymerase genes of BRCA - and POLE -deficient genomes leads to mutations consistent with Sig.#3 and Sig.#10, respectively. However, the genetic mechanisms and potential gene markers for the majority of mutation signatures are still largely unknown.

paragraphs.source: Given its importance in regulating cellular and HIV-1 transcription, targeting BRD4 can be an effective strategy to combat cancer and control HIV latency. To this end, a number of BRD4 inhibitors (called the BET inhibitors or BETi) have been developed and a few tested in clinical trials . The vast majority of them work by disrupting the interaction between the BRD4 BDs and acetyl-lysines. However, these drugs can also act on other BET family members BRD2, BRD3, and BRDT , which all contain the conserved BDs but lack the C-terminal PID and thus cannot functionally substitute for BRD4 in recruiting P-TEFb. In addition, some of the inhibitors affect gene transcription by other unrelated means . The lack of selectivity against BRD4 and the pleiotropic effects of the available BET inhibitors have limited their use in treating BRD4-driven diseases.

Some of the BET inhibitors discovered are BETi or BET inhibitors and a few of them have been tested in clinical trials. Most of them interact with BRD4 BDs and antagonize it by blocking the interaction between the BDs and acetyl-lysines. BRD4 inhibitors, however, can also interact with other BET family members, including BRD2, BRD3 and BRDT that share the BDs but lack C-terminal PID and, thus, cannot replace BRD4 in recruiting P-TEFb. Some of these inhibitors also affect gene transcription by other non-related mechanisms. The lack of selectivity against BRD4 and the pleiotropic effects of currently available BET inhibitors have limited their use in BRD4-driven diseases.

candidates.text: Since BRD4 plays an essential role in controlling the cell life and HIV-1 transcription cycles, targeted therapeutics are a good way to kill cancer cells and combat HIV latency. After a lot of trial and error, multiple BRD4 inhibitors were developed and some of them tested in clinical trials. Although most of them work by inhibiting the interaction between BRD4 BDs and acetyl-lysines, some can also disrupt the interaction between other BETs BRD2, BRD3, and BRDT and BRD4. These BETs have conserved BDs but lack the C-terminal PID and cannot replace BRD4 to recruit and activate P-TEFb. In addition, some of the inhibitors can affect transcription through entirely different mechanisms. However, due to selectivity issues and pleiotropic effects, BRD4-targeting drugs have not been successfully implemented for treating BRD4-driven diseases.
